newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced that individuals would be able to invest 200,000 rand outside South Africa from July 1 -- surprising the markets which had expected 160,000 rand.

- Industrial holdings group New Africa Investments Ltd reported a 47 percent increase in interim headline earnings and announced a one billion rand rights offer of Nail N-shares to finance its additional 5.6 percent stake in Metropolitan Life and other investments.

- Premier Group lifted headline earnings 45 percent to 346.9 million rand in the year to April after a substantial restructuring, lower interest bill and strong performance from its wholesale subsidiary.
- South Africa's annual inflation rate fell to 9.5 percent in May from 9.9 percent in April and Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said he was "very encouraged".
- Resignations in the justice department have continued unabated while only 29 of 187 vacancies for prosecutors, state advocates and state attorneys have been filled this year.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Finance Minster Trevor Manuel was more generous than expected on Wednesday, announcing that South African residents would be allowed to invest 200,000 rand abroad or to hold that amount in foreign currencies in local bank accounts from July 1.

- Wooltru WLOJ.J retail subsidiary Woolworths will take over the 850 million rand debtors' book and responsibility for the future funding of its private-label credit cards from Standard Bank, the company said.

- Competition is intensifying on the home mortgage loan front, with the large commercial banks -- which have generally been losing market share to emerging niche players -- dropping fixed interest rates to attract and keep clients.
SAKE-BEELD
- The government showed its commitment to the final scrapping of exchange controls by announcing a larger limit on individuals' off-shore investments that had been expected.
- Expectations that interest rates could be cut later this year were given a boost with the announcement that the inflation rate decreased last month by more than expected.

- Labour federation Cosatu submitted documents to the Constitutional Court aimed at presenting an appeal against a Labour Court ruling which banned a May 12 protest against the Basic Conditions of Employment bill.
- Black empowerment group New Africa Investments Ltd is raise one billion rand in new capital with a rights issue soon.
THE CITIZEN
- Individual South African taxpayers will be allowed to invest up to 200,000 rand ($44,000) abroad from July 1, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced.
- The government would not abandon its growth, employment and redistribution (GEAR) strategy simply because it was experiencing problems, Manuel said.
- Motorists can expect a three cents a litre drop in the price of petrol when the new adjustment comes into effect on July 2, according to the Automobile Association.
- President Nelson Mandela urged senior South African National Defence Force officers not to take severance packages, but to stay in the force.
- Former state president P.W. Botha said he would never seek amnesty from the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.
--Johannesburg newsroom -27-11-482.1003
